title: Heterogeneous-queue scheduling and KV eviction tuning for mixed-length continuous batching
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: Our continuous batching scheduler is optimized for aggregate throughput but exhibits p95/p99 latency regressions and increased OOM risk when workload mixes short prompts (<=64 tokens) and long responses (>=1024 tokens). Long-response requests inflate KV cache usage during generation, causing GPU memory pressure that increases padding and forces smaller batch windows for other requests.

Goal: Tune the continuous-batching scheduler and KV cache handling so that mixed-length workloads maintain p50/p95 latency SLOs and avoid OOMs while preserving aggregate tokens/sec. Solutions should be deployable to Dedicated and Hosted runtimes and be reversible if regressions occur.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- p95 latency for short-request tail (<=64 prompt tokens) increases by <=10% compared to baseline.
- No production OOMs on target fleet during A/B for 72h.
- Overall token throughput remains within 90% of baseline.
- Observability: per-request KV footprint and per-GPU KV occupancy appear on console dashboard for rollout window.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler exposes heterogeneous queues: short, medium, long, with configurable headroom and per-queue max batch window.
Per-request KV_estimate field implemented (estimated_kv_bytes) and used by scheduler to decide packing and batch admission.
KV eviction policy implemented: soft-eviction first (spill oldest prefix pages to host when safe) and hard-eviction guard to prevent OOMs.
Integration test simulating 50/50 short/long mix runs without OOM for 10k requests and meets latency/throughput SLOs.
Dashboard panels added: kv_bytes_per_request, kv_bytes_per_gpu, scheduler_queue_lengths, and padded_tokens_ratio.
Feature flagged rollout and rollback path documented in rollout_plan field.
Code reviewed and merged; canaryed on 2 nodes for 24h before 10% traffic ramp.
Performance regression test added to CI that replays production trace and checks p95 and GPU memory delta.
Runbook updated for OOM incidents referencing new metrics and the rollback flag.
updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after observing p99 spikes in region-aws-us-west-2; initial triage points to KV growth during generation for long responses.
2026-03-06: Collected 48h trace of requests including prompt_length and response_tokens_actual; sample shows bimodal prompt distribution 60% <=64 tokens, 40% >=256 tokens with heavy tail up to 2048.

2026-03-07: Simulation: replayed trace on staging runtime-1.19 with per-request KV accounting. Observed 2x increase in per-GPU KV occupancy compared to uniform-short workload and increased padding by 18% on average.

2026-03-09: Prototype design: add queue buckets that tag incoming requests into SHORT/MID/LONG by (prompt_len + estimated_response_len). Scheduler calculates candidate batch by KV budget and a soft batch timeout. Implemented KV_estimate RPC field in SDK to allow clients to optionally hint expected response length.

2026-03-10: Spike PR: prototyped soft-eviction where older KV slabs are moved to host memory if GPU headroom < threshold and request is expected to be long. This reduces immediate pressure but increases host-GPU transfer CPU overhead; measurable increase of 5% CPU on the host path.

2026-03-12: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Key feedback: prefer a conservative default that protects short-request latency; avoid aggressive soft-eviction for Dedicated customers unless configured. Decided to make soft-eviction opt-in via release flags and tied to per-node memory headroom heuristics.

2026-03-13: Implemented metrics: estimated_kv_bytes, kv_spill_count, kv_spill_bytes, kv_eviction_count. Added Grafana panels under runtime->kv-cache. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/1581.

2026-03-14: Running canary on staging (2 nodes) with mixed 50/50 trace. Early results: p95 for SHORT queue increased by 6%, overall throughput 92% of baseline, no OOMs. Host CPU increased by ~4% due to spill. Planning broader canary after addressing a race in spill completion.
decisions: Use heterogeneous queueing (3 buckets) instead of single adaptive threshold; simpler to reason about SLA boundaries.
Default behavior: do not enable KV soft-eviction for Hosted customers until we have cost/CPU budget agreement; enable for Dedicated with opt-in toggle.
Accept modest host CPU increase for soft-eviction to avoid GPU OOMs and preserve latency for short requests.
Implement per-request estimated_kv_bytes; allow SDK/clients to supply a hint, but fallback to model-based estimator when absent.
Add a hard eviction emergency path that drops oldest KV segments to prevent OOM if soft-eviction fails, with immediate alerting.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for KV estimator and soft-eviction path. 2) Integration test: run trace replay harness with 10k mixed requests and assert no OOM and SLOs. 3) Canary: deploy to 2 nodes for 24h, collect p50/p95/p99 and memory metrics. 4) Gradual ramp to 10% traffic then 50% if metrics stable.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged. Phase A: staging canary on 2 nodes (done). Phase B: canary on 5 Dedicated nodes with opt-in customers for 72h. Phase C: 10% traffic ramp for hosted for 48h if accepted by product/security. Immediate rollback via runtime flag or scale-to-zero of kv-spill agent.
